# Know Your Strata

> Free compliance calculators for British Columbia strata councils and Ontario condo boards. Every answer cites the section of the statute or regulation it rests on and the date a person last verified it. The sources are re-checked automatically every Monday.

Each tool page states a short answer under its heading, then the calculator, then the full explanation with quoted sections. General information, not legal advice.

## British Columbia (Strata Property Act)

- [AGM / SGM notice calculator](https://knowyourstrata.com/bc/agm-notice): When do we have to send AGM notice? Give at least 2 weeks' written notice of a BC strata AGM or SGM. Counted the legal way, that means sending it no later than 20 days before the meeting by mail, email, fax or mailbox, or 16 days before if it is handed to the person. (Strata Property Act ss. 45(1), 61(3); Interpretation Act ss. 25, 25.2)
- [Special levy calculator](https://knowyourstrata.com/bc/special-levy): How much does each unit owe on our special levy? By default each lot pays its unit entitlement divided by the total entitlement of all lots, approved by a 3/4 vote. Splitting the levy any other fair way, including equally, needs a unanimous vote. (Strata Property Act ss. 99, 108)
- [Quorum calculator](https://knowyourstrata.com/bc/quorum): Do we have quorum for our general meeting? Eligible voters holding 1/3 of the strata corporation's votes, present in person or by proxy, unless your bylaws say otherwise. With fewer than 4 lots or fewer than 4 owners, it is 2/3. (Strata Property Act s. 48(2))
- [Voting threshold checker](https://knowyourstrata.com/bc/voting-threshold): What kind of vote do we need to pass this? It depends on the decision. The Act uses four vote types: a majority or 3/4 of the votes cast by those present, 80% of all eligible voters, or unanimous. Pick your decision to see which one applies and the section that sets it. (Strata Property Act s. 1)
- [Records request deadline](https://knowyourstrata.com/bc/records-deadline): When do we have to answer this records request? Within 2 weeks for most records, within 1 week if the request is only for bylaws or rules, and within 1 week for an Information Certificate (Form B). (Strata Property Act ss. 36, 59)
- [Strata fee / budget calculator](https://knowyourstrata.com/bc/strata-fees): What are each unit's strata fees for this budget? Each lot pays the approved budget in proportion to its unit entitlement: its own entitlement divided by the total entitlement of all lots. Two lots in the same building usually pay different amounts. (Strata Property Act ss. 99, 246)
- [CRF contribution checker](https://knowyourstrata.com/bc/crf-contribution): Does our CRF contribution meet the legal minimum? At least 10% of the amount budgeted for the operating fund, every year, with no exception for a large existing balance. (Strata Property Act s. 93; Strata Property Regulation ss. 3.4, 6.1)
- [Insurance deductible — who pays](https://knowyourstrata.com/bc/insurance-deductible): Who pays the insurance deductible? By default the strata corporation pays it, as a common expense through strata fees. The strata can sue an owner to recover the deductible if the owner is responsible for the loss, and your bylaws can change what it has to prove. (Strata Property Act s. 158)
- [Fine & enforcement procedure](https://knowyourstrata.com/bc/fine-enforcement-procedure): Was the fine procedure followed correctly? Only if, before fining, the strata received a complaint, gave the owner or tenant the particulars in writing, and gave a reasonable chance to answer, including a hearing if one was requested. A fine imposed without those steps is open to challenge. (Strata Property Act s. 135)
- [Meeting minutes generator](https://knowyourstrata.com/bc/meeting-minutes-generator): Strata Council Meeting Minutes Generator. Minutes are required for every general and council meeting and must record the results of any votes. The Act sets no format, which is the gap this generator fills. (Strata Property Act s. 35(1)(a); Standard Bylaw 18(3))
- [Depreciation report deadline](https://knowyourstrata.com/bc/depreciation-report-deadline): When is our strata's depreciation report due? Every BC strata with 5 or more lots must obtain a depreciation report every 5 years, and the option to defer it by vote is gone. Stratas with 4 or fewer lots are exempt, and first deadlines phase in by region. (Strata Property Act s. 94; Strata Property Regulation s. 6.21)

## Ontario (Condominium Act, 1998)

- [Quorum calculator](https://knowyourstrata.com/on/quorum): Do we have quorum for this meeting of owners? Owners of 25% of the units. It drops to 15% only on a third attempt at an AGM, and parking, storage and service units are left out of the count. (Condominium Act, 1998 s. 50; O. Reg. 48/01 s. 1.1)
- [Notice of meeting deadline](https://knowyourstrata.com/on/notice-of-meeting-deadline): When do we have to send meeting notice? Send the Preliminary Notice at least 20 days before the Notice of Meeting, and the Notice of Meeting at least 15 days before the meeting, so start at least 35 days out. (Condominium Act, 1998 ss. 45.1, 47(1))
- [Requisition threshold checker](https://knowyourstrata.com/on/requisition-threshold): How many owners do we need to requisition a meeting? Under the current section 46, owners of at least 15% of the units can requisition a meeting, not counting parking, storage or service units. A requisition received on or after December 31, 2026 follows the new section 46 instead. (Condominium Act, 1998 s. 46; O. Reg. 48/01 ss. 1.1, 80)
- [Records request deadline](https://knowyourstrata.com/on/records-request-deadline): When do we have to answer this records request? The board must respond within 30 days of receiving the request, saying whether it will allow access and what the fee is. Delivering the records can run on a second clock. (O. Reg. 48/01 s. 13.3(6))
- [Reserve fund study deadline](https://knowyourstrata.com/on/reserve-fund-study-deadline): When is our next reserve fund study due, and what class must it be? The first study, always comprehensive, is due within the year after the declaration is registered. After that, a new study is due within every three years of completing the last one. (Condominium Act, 1998 s. 94(4); O. Reg. 48/01 ss. 27, 28)
- [Status certificate deadline](https://knowyourstrata.com/on/status-certificate-deadline): When is our status certificate due, and what happens if we are late? Within 10 days after the corporation has both the request and the fee, counted from whichever arrived later. If it is late, the Act deems a certificate given in the buyer's favour, and the fee is capped at $100 including tax. (Condominium Act, 1998 s. 76(3), (5), (6); O. Reg. 48/01 s. 18(4))
- [Voting threshold checker](https://knowyourstrata.com/on/voting-threshold): What vote do we actually need? It depends on the decision. A by-law needs owners of a majority of all units, a substantial change to the common elements needs 66 2/3% of all units, and a declaration amendment needs 80% or 90% written consent. (Condominium Act, 1998 ss. 56(10), 97(4), 107(2))
- [Insurance deductible chargeback](https://knowyourstrata.com/on/insurance-deductible): Can we charge the deductible back to the owner? Automatically, only for damage to the owner's own unit caused by the owner, their lessee or someone living there with their permission, and only up to the lesser of the repair cost and the deductible. Other damage stays a common expense unless a by-law under s. 105(3) says otherwise. (Condominium Act, 1998 s. 105)
- [Common expense calculator](https://knowyourstrata.com/on/common-expense-calculator): How much does each unit pay toward the common expenses? In the proportions your declaration sets out. The Act has no default formula and no deemed equal split, so the declaration governs. (Condominium Act, 1998 s. 84(1))
- [Lien deadline calculator](https://knowyourstrata.com/on/lien-deadline): How long do we have to register the lien? Register a certificate of lien within three months of the default or the lien expires, and give the owner at least 10 days' written notice before you register. (Condominium Act, 1998 s. 85(2), (4))
- [AGM deadline](https://knowyourstrata.com/on/agm-deadline): When must our Ontario condo hold its AGM? Within six months of the end of each fiscal year. A new corporation holds its first meeting of owners within three months of registration. (Condominium Act, 1998 s. 45(2))
- [Information certificate deadline](https://knowyourstrata.com/on/information-certificate-deadline): When is our periodic information certificate due? Within 60 days after the end of the first and the third quarter of the fiscal year. The second and fourth quarters have no certificate of their own unless a by-law adds one. (Condominium Act, 1998 s. 26.3; O. Reg. 48/01 s. 11.1(4))

## Guides

- [What changes for Ontario condo boards on December 31, 2026](https://knowyourstrata.com/on/december-31-2026-changes): the new requisition process (prescribed form, 20 day board answer, 40 day meeting clock), the reserved seat moving to non-leased voting units, and which date decides (O. Reg. 48/01 ss. 79 to 81)
